overview: Lilly's Q2 revenue grew 48% year over year, with MOUNJARO and ZEPBOUND contributing $14.9B (+$6.3B) and non-GAAP EPS of $8.38 including $3.03 of acquired IPR&D charges, versus $6.31 a year ago. Lucas Montarce, CFO, raised full-year revenue guidance to $85B-$87B from $82B-$85B and the performance margin range to 49%-50.5%. Dave Ricks, Chair and CEO, said that while Lilly is pleased with progress, "we're not satisfied".
keyTakeaways: Ilya Yuffa, President of Lilly USA, said U.S. Foundayo volume almost doubled in the last week of July versus a month earlier, with about one in four new starts and prescribers up from about 8,000 to 36,000.
Dave Ricks, Chair and CEO, said retatrutide's BLA classification is in active litigation with the FDA, with submission expected by Q1 2027 once more CMC data are gathered.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Program launched July 1 for 20 million eligible Americans at $50 a month; Yuffa said around 80% of early patients are on injectables and 60%-70% are new to treatment.
Lucas Montarce, CFO, said ZEPBOUND net price will go down "for sure" as CVS access resumes in Q4, embedded in the guide and more than offset by volume.
financialHighlights: Revenue up 48%; U.S. revenue up 33% on volume, with U.S. price down 3% (down 9% excluding rebate estimate changes).
Constant-currency growth of 55% in Europe (including a $250M Jardiance milestone), 30% in Japan, 93% in China and 136% in rest of world.
Gross margin 86.3%, up about 1.3 points; marketing, selling and administrative up 25%; R&D up 14% with more than 40 phase III programs.
Non-GAAP performance margin 54.8%, up nine points; Ebglyss sales more than doubled and Jaypirca grew 56%.
guidance: Lucas Montarce, CFO, raised full-year revenue to $85B-$87B from $82B-$85B, a $2.5B midpoint increase, with second-half growth significant in dollars but slower in percentage terms.
Montarce raised the non-GAAP performance margin to 49%-50.5% from 47%-48.5% and set non-GAAP EPS at $35.50-$36.50, up $2.78 at the midpoint before the $3.03 Q2 acquired IPR&D charge.
Montarce said prior-period rebate adjustments will not recur in the second half, which also carries Europe Q3 and U.S. Type 2 diabetes Q4 seasonality.

Dave Ricks, Chair and CEO, expects Foundayo U.S. Type 2 diabetes action later this year; Patrik Jonsson, President of Lilly International, expects the major OUS rollout at the beginning of 2027; Dan Skovronsky, Chief Scientific and Product Officer, expects the retatrutide submission in Q1 2027.
risksMentioned: Foundayo's U.S. launch curve was slower than anticipated, and the inflection claim rests on a few weeks of data.
ZEPBOUND net price is expected to fall from Q4 as CVS access resumes and medical exceptions fade, per Montarce.
Retatrutide's BLA pathway is disputed with the FDA, with a mixed first court decision, per Ricks.
Novo Nordisk's oral is scaling in the U.K., Germany and the UAE and generic semaglutide has launched in India and Brazil, per Jonsson.

qa.question: Why has the U.S. Foundayo launch been slower than anticipated, when will it inflect, and how is the ex-U.S. race against Novo's oral shaping up?
qa.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
qa.answer: CVS added Foundayo in June, Bridge launched July 1 and full DTC began; in the last week of July volume almost doubled with about one in four new starts on Foundayo. Patrik Jonsson, President of Lilly International: the UAE launch started strongly and Lilly held incretin share despite a second oral; Mexico and Saudi Arabia are next, most launches in 2027.
qa.read: Answered partially; called Novo's share claim noisy sell-in data.

qa.question: What milestones remain for retatrutide under the BLA pathway, and will the classification apply to later incretins?
qa.answer: Lilly holds retatrutide is a biologic under the amino acid count rule; the first court decision was mixed and litigation is active. All clinical data are in hand, more CMC data must be gathered, and submission is expected by Q1 next year.
qa.read: Answered partially; later incretins not addressed.

qa.question: Guidance implies a second-half deceleration despite Bridge and Foundayo access; is price being missed or is the team conservative?
qa.answer: The guide rose $2.5B; recent quarters included one-off rebate adjustments that will not continue, the 2025 base had a bolus of new-country MOUNJARO launches that will not repeat, and Europe Q3 and U.S. Type 2 diabetes Q4 seasonality are factored in; second-half dollar growth is still significant.

qa.question: ZEPBOUND net price looks like about $580 per prescription, well above cash prices; how sustainable is the medical-exception delta now CVS is back?
qa.answer: LillyDirect runs $299 to $449, Bridge $245, plus the commercial price; medical exceptions and larger commercial script sizes lift the per-prescription figure. CVS access resumes in Q4, medical exceptions are "maybe a short-term thing", and price is expected to go down for sure, embedded in the guide.
qa.read: Answered partially; no net price figure.

unanswered.question: Is Foundayo sampling dampening weekly IQVIA prescription data?
unanswered.how: Ilya Yuffa, President of Lilly USA, described the sampling program and prescriber count but did not say whether it dampens the data.

unanswered.question: Are psychiatry and vaccines scalable priorities or one-off deals?
unanswered.how: Jake Van Naarden, President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development, would not forward-look, saying Lilly will be opportunistic.

unanswered.question: Will BLA classification apply to subsequent incretins?
unanswered.how: Dave Ricks, Chair and CEO, addressed only retatrutide.
